findings.evidence: The compiled guess card contains the example ‘격식 있는 자리에서는 천천히 말합니다.’ but has target:null. GuessCard.svelte therefore displays only the dictionary form ‘말하다’, so the learner receives no sentence context for choosing among ‘to start’, ‘to speak; to say’, and ‘to end; to be over’. If the target is repaired, all three verbs also fit ‘격식 있는 자리에서는 천천히 ___’ naturally.
findings.fix: Added a failing regression first, repaired guessTarget, and confirmed the recompiled target is 말합; the associated distractor bans in data/overrides.json remove the reported alternatives.

findings.evidence: The card shows ‘발표 끝났어요.’ with ‘to end; to be over’ and ‘to start’. ‘발표 시작했어요’ is an equally natural sentence, so context cannot distinguish the offered opposite verbs.
findings.fix: Applied the concrete mutual distractor bans in data/overrides.json and confirmed after recompilation that the quoted card no longer offers the reported alternative meanings.

findings.evidence: The key point says, ‘When unsure, use 해요체 — it's polite and never rude.’ This absolute contradicts the same chapter’s statements that a grammatically polite sentence can still sound cold or awkward and that setting, wording, and attitude affect appropriateness.
findings.fix: Qualified the local 해요체 guidance as the usual conversational default while preserving the role of wording, tone, and formal setting, then confirmed the recompiled teaching text.

findings.evidence: The pronunciation note says, ‘In 반말 questions, the rising pitch alone marks the question ... There's no -까? ending and no spelling change.’ This overgeneralizes one 가./가? pair: casual Korean also has overt question endings such as -니? and -(으)ㄹ까?.
findings.fix: Scoped the local intonation rule to unmarked pairs such as 가./가? and acknowledged -니? and -(으)ㄹ까?, then confirmed the recompiled pronunciation note.

findings.evidence: QA 1 answers ‘지금부터 발표를 시작하겠습니다라고 말할 거예요.’ The polite sentence ending is attached directly to 라고 without direct-quotation marks; the reading itself correctly uses ‘“지금부터 발표를 시작하겠습니다”라고’.
findings.fix: Corrected the local QA answer to “지금부터 발표를 시작하겠습니다”라고 말할 거예요. and confirmed the recompiled reading card matches the quoted source sentence.

findings.evidence: The source has ‘“질문 있으십니까?”라고’, but the compiled read chunk contains ‘“질문 있으십니까? ”라고’ with an inserted space before the closing quotation mark. buildReadingBite splits at ? before consuming the closing quote and then joins the pieces with a space.
findings.fix: Added a failing reading-segmentation regression first, repaired buildReadingBite, and confirmed the recompiled chunk preserves “질문 있으십니까?”라고 without inserted whitespace.
